description: The episode prompt for the repetition pass: one JSON object per episode, sent first in the user turn. Steps are sampled at a fixed interval from the three video topics of one trimmed delivery MCAP (data/trimmed/episode_NNNNNN.mcap, 14_trim_mcap_common_span.py: the three views start and end within one frame, so the cameras of a step show the same instant). Camera roles come from the MCAP metadata: /cameras/camera0 = right wrist (robot0), camera1 = left wrist (robot1), camera2 = head. The images follow in the order of 'images', each preceded by '<image id> | camera <camera> | t = <t_s> s | step <n>'. The steps are the fixed grid the model must answer in; it never builds its own step numbering, so code can map every step to a timestamp. Steps are sampled frames, not every frame: the model should not assume actions between steps that the images do not show. No sensor timeline is included: the model counts repetitions from video only. The model identifies the task from the three views and counts the cycles (repetitions) of that task in this episode.

context.rig: MCAP metadata recording.robot_type (umi_bimanual); 'UMI handheld rig' when unset
context.duration_s: episode length in seconds: recording.episode_length / video_fps (59.94)
context.given_task: task text of the delivery order for this task folder (e.g. task01), when one was given; null when none. A hint, not a fact: the model describes what the images show

views.head: head-mounted, forward facing: scene, object and destination locations, overall task progress
views.wrist_left: left gripper camera: left-hand grasp, contact, manipulation and release
views.wrist_right: right gripper camera: right-hand grasp, contact, manipulation and release
views.missing_views: image_order lists only the views actually sent (head only for a head MP4); the model uses the remaining views and does not invent the missing ones
